sources.title: Grand Theft Auto VI launches tomorrow, November 19
sources.text: The latest installment in the Grand Theft Auto series heads to the state of Leonida, home to the neon-soaked streets of Vice City and beyond. Jason and Lucia have always known the deck is stacked against them. But when an easy score goes wrong, they find themselves on the darkest side of the sunniest place in America, in the middle of a criminal conspiracy stretching across the state of Leonida — forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive. Grand Theft Auto VI arrives on PlayStation 5 Thursday, November 19, available at PlayStation Store. The game is set in the state of Leonida, home to the neon-soaked streets of Vice City and beyond in the biggest, most immersive evolution of the series yet. Jason grew up around grifters and crooks. After a stint in the Army trying to shake off his troubled teens, he found himself in the Keys doing what he knows best, working for local drug runners. Meeting Lucia could be the best or worst thing to ever happen to him. Jason knows how he’d like it to turn out but right now, it’s hard to tell. Lucia’s father taught her to fight as soon as she could walk, and life has been coming at her swinging ever since. Fighting for her family landed her in the Leonida Penitentiary. Sheer luck got her out but now more than anything, Lucia wants the good life her mom has dreamed of since their days in Liberty City. Instead of half-baked fantasies, Lucia is prepared to take matters into her own hands. Leonida is made up of six regions: Vice City, the Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia, and Mount Kalaga. Here’s a closer look at what makes each region unique. The glamour, hustle, and greed of America captured in a single city. Each neighborhood has something to offer, from the pastel art deco hotels and bright white sands of Ocean Beach, to the bustling panaderías of Little Cuba and the bootleg brands of the Tisha-Wocka flea market, out to the VC Port, the cruise ship capital of the world. We’re a long way from the ’80s, but Vice City is still the sun and fun capital of America Life in this tropical archipelago isn’t flashy but it’s easy. Get your buzz on and pull up a deck chair but look out — you are right on the doorstep of some of the most beautiful and dangerous waters in all of America. You never know what lies beneath the surface of this primordial expanse. The gators may be the most famous attraction, but there are far deadlier predators and weirder discoveries among the mangroves. Cheap motels, shut-down attractions, and empty strip malls won’t bring the tourists back, but there’s a new economy in this once-popular vacation spot. It’s fueled by malt liquor, painkillers, and truck stop energy drinks. In the heart of Leonida, American industry and old school values still reign supreme — whatever the cost. The Allied Crystal sugar refinery provides the jobs, while the local biker gang provides almost everything else. A national landmark up against the state’s northern border, Mount Kalaga offers prime hunting, fishing, and off-road trails. In the lush surrounding backwoods, hillbilly mystics and paranoid radicals live far from the prying eyes of the government. Spanning stations including Classic Rock, Modern Hip-Hop, Pop, Metal, Dance, Latin, ‘80s, Electronic, Blues, Ballads, Talk Radio, and much more, Grand Theft Auto VI features the biggest and widest-ranging selection of in-game radio yet. Plus, for the first time ever, Grand Theft Auto VI introduces a series of on-demand podcasts for Jason and Lucia to experience beyond Leonida’s terrestrial radio, with both radio and podcasts available to listen to in vehicles and on foot through newly introduced headphones and earbuds connected to their smartphones.

sources.text: O mais novo título da série Grand Theft Auto nos leva ao estado de Leonida, até as ruas iluminadas de neon de Vice City e além. Jason e Lucia sempre souberam que as cartas não estavam a favor deles. Mas quando o que deveria ser um trabalho fácil dá errado, eles se encontram no lado mais escuro do lugar mais ensolarado da América, no meio de uma conspiração criminosa que cobre todo o estado de Leonida, forçados a depender um do outro mais do que nunca se quiserem sair vivos. Grand Theft Auto VI chega para PlayStation 5 quinta-feira, 19 de novembro, disponível na PlayStation Store. O jogo se passa no estado de Leonida, onde ficam as ruas banhadas de neon de Vice City e além, na maior e mais imersiva evolução da série até hoje. Jason cresceu rodeado de bandidos e vigaristas. Após um período no exército para tentar se livrar de sua adolescência perturbada, ele se encontra nos Keys fazendo o que faz melhor, trabalhando para traficantes de drogas locais. Conhecer Lucia pode ser a melhor ou a pior coisa que já aconteceu com ele. Jason sabe como gostaria que tudo terminasse, mas agora, é difícil prever. O pai de Lucia a ensinou a lutar desde que ela aprendeu a andar, e a vida tem vindo com tudo para cima dela desde então. Lutar por sua família a colocou na Penitenciária de Leonida. Sorte pura a livrou desta vez, mas agora mais do que qualquer coisa, Lucia deseja a vida boa com a qual sua mãe sonhava desde que moravam em Liberty City. Em vez de fantasias pela metade, Lucia está preparada para assumir o controle da situação. Leonida é composto de seis regiões: Vice City, as Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia, e Mount Kalaga. Vamos conhecer o que torna cada região única. O glamour, o trabalho e a ganância da América capturados em uma única cidade. Cada bairro tem algo a oferecer, dos hóteis de art deco, cores pastel e areia branca de Ocean Beach, até as padarias de Little Cuba e as marcas falsificadas do mercadinho de Tisha-Wocka, até o VC Port, a capital mundial dos navios de cruzeiro. Estamos longe dos anos 80, mas Vice City ainda é a capital do sol e da diversão da América. A vida neste arquipélago tropical não é chamativa, mas é boa. Pegue uma cervejinha e puxe uma cadeira de praia, mas tome cuidado, você está à beira das águas mais belas e perigosas da América. Você nunca sabe o que está sob a superfície desta região primordial. Os jacarés podem ser a atração mais famosa, mas há predadores bem mais perigosos e descobertas mais estranhas entre o manguezal. Motéis baratos, atrações fechadas, e galerias de lojas vazias e abandonadas não vão trazer os turistas de volta, mas há uma nova economia neste local que já foi um ponto turístico. Agora mandam o as bebidas baratas, remédios contra a dor e bebidas energéticas. No coração de Leonida, a indústria Americana e os antigos valores ainda reinam supremos, seja qual for o custo. A refinaria de açúcar Allied Crystal providencia os empregos, e a gangue de motociclistas local providencia quase todo o resto. Um marco nacional na fronteira norte do estado, Mount Kalaga oferece as melhores trilhas off-road e pontos de pesca e caça. Nas florestas em torno, caipiras místicos e radicais paranóicos vivem longe dos olhos vigilantes do governo. Com estações de Rock Clássico, Hip-Hop Moderno, Pop, Metal, Dance, Latina, Anos 80, Electrônica, Blues, Baladas, Talk Radio, e muito mais, Grand Theft Auto VI possui a maior e mais variada seleção de rádios em um jogo até hoje. Além disso, pela primeira vez, Grand Theft Auto VI apresenta uma série de podcasts sob demanda para Jason e Lucia ouvirem além das rádios de Leonida, com ambos disponíveis para ouvir em veículos e a pé usando fones de ouvido e earbuds conectados aos seus smartphones.

sources.title: What if Vampire Survivors met Grand Theft Auto 2? Maniac is a brilliant mash-up that dares to ask that question
sources.text: "We all have a pathetic hot-dog-suit guy inside of us." What would you get if you combined the chaotic top-down action of old-school Grand Theft Auto 2 with the chaotic top-down action of Vampire Survivors? That's the question Soldat and King Arthur's Gold developer Transhuman asked when it started working on 2024's roguelite shooter Maniac. The result is a delight, yet Maniac remains frustratingly underappreciated. Your goal is simple: survive for as long as you can or until the 20-minute clock hits zero. Throughout that time, your secondary objective is to create as much mayhem as possible - painting the road with the blood of your foes, slamming cars into buildings, performing drive-bys as you rampage across the procedurally-generated city. The more carnage you cause, the higher your Wanted level, until you're fending off police and the military. Maniac's debt to GTA is clear, and its chaotic action is brilliantly realised as it channels the compelling rhythms of a Survivors-style roguelite, where randomness in items and level layout makes each run fresh as you strive to unlock new characters, progressing a little further each time. It's a relatively slight experience, as its £4 price tag reflects, featuring a single compact map, just six characters, and barely any permanent progression. But Maniac makes a spirited argument for a return to a simpler time when GTA was all about shooting cops, stealing cars, and indiscriminately murdering pedestrians rather than the 'everything' game it is today. Maniac is also a game that feels like it's trying to make good on an idea many of us had when we first played GTA 1 & 2 all those years ago: what would a better-looking, more advanced version of that look like? And for developer Michał Marcinkowski, Maniac's genesis also harkens back to an earlier time. "When I was 12, I used to come back from school and play the demo of GTA 1," he tells me over email. "It was top-down and time-limited, and all I'd do was try to cause as much chaos as possible within the 20 minutes of the demo." And there's perhaps a hint of a 12-year-old's exuberance to Maniac. There's the bright colour palette and gleeful chaos of its physics-driven mechanics, the adrenaline rush its aggressive enemy AI creates, and its absurd roster of playable characters, which range from Little Girl to Hotdog Guy. "Each [character] is a bit of me and a bit of you," Marcinkowski explains. "We all have a drunk Santa in us. We all have a pathetic hot-dog-suit guy inside of us. Each character failed at something and is lashing out." As each new Grand Theft Auto game pushes further into realism, the idea of recreating the rampages seen in classic GTA feels increasingly unpalatable, but Maniac's colourful cartoon aesthetic means it can get away with more. One Achievement, with a flourish of old-school bad-taste humour, challenges players to destroy five school buses using an airstrike ability called Santa's Little Helpers. And that level of irreverent, chaotic lunacy escalates the deeper into each session you get, particularly as your Wanted level climbs: if you antagonise law enforcement enough here, they eventually break out a game-ending nuke. "This comes back to being 12," Marcinkowski says. "Nukes are just cool. I wanted the game to end with a bang, and what's more maniacal and exaggerated than a nuke? So that idea was with me for more than 20 years." Core to Maniac's design is the ability to change from a Survivors-like auto-shooter to a standard shooter where you're able to control your aim. The latter option is, I think, the more fitting one, particularly given how much driving you do. If you squint, it almost feels like a GTA 2 clone. And while the Vampire Survivors inspirations are plentiful - including its now-standard three-option upgrade system - the GTA elements are clearly the more prevalent. It might not play exactly like a GTA game, but it certainly captures the series' early days spirit. And Marcinkowski says he's surprised more developers haven't tried to riff on GTA: "You'd expect the most popular game in the world to have hundreds of clones, but that's not the case." There may be a reason for that. As big as modern-day GTA is, clones are apparently much less popular. "When you look at the sales data, particularly of top-down GTA clones, they don't sell well", explains Marcinkowski. "I found that out way too late, and I thought Maniac wouldn't be a hit." His publisher was initially equally buoyant too. "But then they studied the market and stopped being so hyped. That's how it felt as we got close to release. The wishlist count wasn't very high." "I was expecting 10,000 [copies sold]," Marcinkowski tells me. "I actually started making another game two months before Maniac came out because I thought I'd go broke." But then the game launched, and early worries proved unfounded. It sold more than 100K copies, comfortably blowing past its maker's modest expectations, putting it in the top one percent of games released on Steam. It's a surprise success story built on the foundations of Marcinkowski's youth, and as we chat about GTA, he reveals he's less keen on Rockstar's modern games, which lack that classic gameplay drive. "I always liked the counter-culture side of GTA, which is why I put so much of it into Maniac," he elaborates. " GTA 6 seems to have become pop culture, so it's lost its appeal for me." Marcinkowski's heart, it seems, is old-school.

sources.title: Expedition 33 lead writer says Grand Theft Auto 6 layoff concerns show that 'people creating the value do not receive a proportionate amount of that value'
sources.text: "I sincerely hope the Rockstar team is successful in unionizing". Grand Theft Auto 6 is already enormously successful, having enjoyed "the biggest entertainment launch in history" . But the current games industry is such that some Rockstar developers are still concerned about being laid off in the wake of its release. Writing for the Guardian prior to GTA 6 's launch, Rockstar animation programmer Nestor Uriarte explained that although there is "no indication that layoffs are coming" it nonetheless "says a lot about the industry that even my colleagues and I, working on the biggest game of all time, are worried about getting laid off." It might sound odd for the developers of such a hugely successful game to be worried about losing their jobs, but layoffs don't just occur when games or companies struggle commercially. A common cause of layoffs in the games industry is companies trying to reduce overheads after a game has launched, as the studio switches from full production to post-release support for their current game and planning for the next one. It's partly why the industry seems to be in a constant, rolling state of layoffs, even when games appear to sell well. This issue was recently addressed by Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, the lead writer of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 . Svedberg-Yen, who left Sandfall Interactive in July , claimed that the problem is exacerbated by an imbalance in who benefits financially when a game like Grand Theft Auto 6 launches. "99 Metacritic score. Multiple award nominations before it even released. Massive sales and player engagement. Incredible amounts of tangible and intangible value creation. Yet the team is worried about layoffs," Svedberg-Yen wrote in an Instagram post. "So, who receives the lion's share of the profits from their labor? Not the vast majority of the creative team." Svedberg-Yen pointed out that this is "one of the issues that happens when the people creating the value do not receive a proportionate amount of that value," adding that "In finance, we call that value extraction." Svedberg-Yen also commented on the Rockstar team's ongoing efforts to unionise, with the team in the process of voting on whether or not it wants a union. If successful, the Rockstar Game Workers Union would become the biggest in the UK's gaming sector. "I sincerely hope the Rockstar team is successful in unionizing," Svedberg-Yen wrote. "Layoffs during lulls in development cycles would work a lot better if teams were properly paid for the value they create, not just one-time, but throughout the life of the thing they created." sources.title: Jason's stoic character in Grand Theft Auto 6 was inspired by Steve McQueen and research into Army veterans: 'These guys typically aren't running their mouths'
sources.text: Rockstar made a point of creating "authentic characters that didn't stray too far from reality." It's already clear that Grand Theft Auto 6 has a very different timbre than most other GTA games. While criminal hijinks and acerbic satire remain part of the experience, it's also much more interested in portraying characters and relationships in a more convincing, human fashion. One of the most striking examples of this is its depiction of co-protagonist Jason Duval, who, unlike the vast majority of GTA's main characters, is often notable for what he doesn't say rather than what he does. According to Rockstar's senior vice president of narrative Rupert Humphries, Jason's laconic nature was inspired by a personality type observed in both cinema and real-life. "When we decided we wanted to tell a story about a couple on the run, we looked at all the similar kinds of movies, and one of the ones that really stood out was [Sam] Peckinpah's The Getaway" Humphries explained in a statement given to Destructoid (via GamesRadar ). Steve McQueen was famous for pulling lines out of scripts and saying things with his presence alone. We wanted to see how close we could get to that with a game character, where so many of our protagonists have been the opposite." Humphries says this also "resonated" with research the studio was doing around Army veterans, particularly Army Rangers. In Grand Theft Auto 6 , Duval is a veteran of the game's equivalent military organisation called the Marauders. "These guys typically aren't running their mouths or reacting to something unless it's strictly necessary, while still being strong and still asserting themselves," Humphries explained. Establishing a more grounded character was not solely a directive for Jason. It was a goal of the writing more broadly. This is interesting considering Florida was picked as the setting for GTA 6 in-part due to the wild 'Florida Man' stories that circulate on the Internet from the state. "Researching the prolific and headline-grabbing criminal activity that had been taking place over decades in Florida was an obvious starting point," game writer Michael Wiafe pointed out. "From then on, it was about coming up with authentic characters that didn't stray too far from reality but also were not totally bound by it either," Wiafe continues. "The majority of our main characters are undeniably reprehensible on paper, full-blown criminals, but also decent human beings. Their moral makeup isn’t necessarily cut-and-dry, and we don’t attempt to make excuses for them. What's important is how they resonate, no matter where you're experiencing the game in the world." This is just one of the things that makes Rockstar's latest crime sim a marvel on pretty much all fronts . And while us PC gamers will have to wait an unspecified amount of time before it arrives on the platform, you can bet it going to be quite the experience when it does. sources.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 has a 'complex drug network' that tracks everything from where drugs come from to 'how they eventually reach the street-level buyer'
sources.text: "Having that structure in the background as something we consistently refer to helps everything feel more real." I've only dipped my toe into Grand Theft Auto 6 thus far, but I'm already impressed by the detail Rockstar has baked into its world. One thing I'm always curious about with games like this, however, is how much of that detail is on the surface versus what's actually happening under the hood. I'm still too early in the game to judge this for myself, but according to Rockstar, there is way more going on in terms of how NPCs behave than players will ever likely see. One striking example of this is how GTA 6 's gang compounds conduct their drug operations. In an interview with IGN , Rockstar's senior design director for its open world Steven Messinger explained that GTA 6 fully simulates drug distribution from top to bottom. "A big part of [the open world's design] was establishing deep backstories for almost everything, even if they were never meant to be fully explained to the player, and then really sticking to those backstories," Messinger pointed out. "For example, our gang compounds have a complex drug network we've fully mapped out: where the drugs come from, who brings them in and how, how they're distributed to each compound, what happens at each stop, and how they eventually reach the street-level buyer." Messinger notes that "players will only pick up bits and pieces of this". But representing this process wholesale means that, when players do notice it, it always feels authentic and believable. "Having that structure in the background as something we consistently refer to helps everything feel more real, like this big machine is always running even when players aren't there." While this may only be designed for players to notice passively, I'm now keen to follow this system and see just how consistently it holds up. sources.title: How Rockstar Made Every NPC Feel Alive in GTA 6
sources.text: Game developers often refer to their open world cities as characters due to the sheer craftsmanship involved in building out a believable, diverse playspace for the player with its own districts, history, and architecture. This is truer for GTA 6 than most games, but what makes Leonida really feel alive — outside of the puddles of bin juice, the regional-specific cop cars, and mapped out power grid — are the people who live there. GTA 6 feels like a massive evolution in what it means to be a non-player character (NPC) because there’s an emphasis on the “C” — they’re actually characters in their own right. NPCs don’t just all look unique — with body types, skin, dress style, and hair making them stand apart — they have their own personalities and temperaments. Start a fight with one NPC and they might fight back, while another runs away. One could start a fight by slapping you, another might flick their cigarette at you or tip their drink over your head. Passersby can cheer the fight on, flee, or get involved. Some stop after a single punch knocks sense into them, while others swing until they’re out cold . No matter where you go in GTA 6, it feels like a lived-in world, on the macro and micro scale. There are over 100 interiors to explore, and each house tells you a story about its occupants. Listen to conversations out on the streets and you’ll get a window into their minds, built out by an entire Rockstar studio dedicated to making them authentic and believable, while still being larger-than-life, funny, and often unhinged. “A big part of it was establishing deep backstories for almost everything, even if they were never meant to be fully explained to the player, and then really sticking to those backstories,” said Steven Messinger, Rockstar's senior design director for the open world. “For example, our gang compounds have a complex drug network we’ve fully mapped out: where the drugs come from, who brings them in and how, how they’re distributed to each compound, what happens at each stop, and how they eventually reach the street-level buyer. “Players will only pick up on bits and pieces of this, but having that structure in the background as something we consistently refer to helps everything feel more real, like this big machine is always running even when players aren’t there.” To build this tangible sense of place, Rockstar takes in-depth research trips for GTA games , embedding the writers in the mundane and the more extreme to really capture the soul of a city. Helicopter trips of the Florida Keys, ride-alongs with police, talking to people, taking photos and notes, all build up a snapshot that Rockstar bottles up to digitize in video game format. “We had a lot of fun trying to capture the raw energy and vibrant chaos that Florida is known for,” said senior design director of world and population, John Macpherson. “By immersing ourselves into a number of these locations on reference trips, spending time with locals, experiencing as much as possible firsthand, we gathered a direct sense of what would make Leonida feel truly alive. “Everywhere you look, little stories constantly unfold. It could be as simple as what someone’s wearing, how fit they are, how they walk and talk, who they’re with, what tunes they’re blasting as they cruise down the street. We tried to match that in-game as much as possible, hopefully resulting in something that feels full of life.” You can walk along Vice Beach and see sugar daddies with their trophy wives, locals playing volleyball, tourists sunbathing, and people walking their pets. Everywhere you look, there’s something happening in Leonida, and it’s completely enveloping. You feel like a part of its world, rather than a godlike being with total control over it. There’s a mission around the midpoint of the game where protagonists Jason and Lucia people-watch from a hotel sunbed, inventing backstories for the guests by the pool, and it’s something I found myself doing as I explored the world and passed people by, such is the variety and diversity of the game’s NPCs. No other game has ever had such a colorful cast of extras, which is wild when you consider all this was built to add credibility to a world you can zoom past at 100mph. “We evolved from monolithic NPCs built to visual standards that were lower than the main cast in GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2, to fully fleshed-out characters with singular awareness and visual identities,” said Valmor Garcia, senior technical art director on GTA 6. “They are driven by dynamic moods, personalities, unique anatomy, facial features, and dialogue that are visually on par with our protagonists, Jason and Lucia.” Rockstar built entirely new technology for GTA 6 to simulate hair, cloth, and the way muscles move under the skin. All that work is implemented equally across all characters, so there’s never that uncanny moment where you come face-to-face with a flat and lifeless NPC, staring at you with dead eyes. Everyone you meet is equally detailed, and the range of visual design is staggering. Of course, this approach created challenges in other areas of development. It’s fairly straightforward to implement a combat system in a game where all character models are approximately the same size, but the varied body types of GTA 6 meant Rockstar had to take a look at how it approached animations so physical contact looks good no matter how big or small the character models are. Especially since this is a game where the two leads can also change in size through diet and exercise . “We decided early on that we wanted to really push the variation in character sizes and body types,” vice president of animation, Mark Tennant, explained. “This required us to establish a very robust way to share animations between characters while still resolving multiple points of contact, such as most vehicle interactions and grappling in hand-to-hand combat. “Developing this workflow meant that we needed our animators to adopt new tec

sources.title: How to steal the BF Bandito in GTA 6
sources.text: Track down this white off-roader for Moses. The BF Bandito is one of the many cars in GTA 6 that Moses asks you to steal and bring to him for cold, hard cash. This one has a search area out in Buskin Swamp, but when you arrive it's not immediately clear where or how to steal the car. The owner of this white offroad racer will drive around the map marked search area in a circle, as shown in the clip above. To get him to stop, simply park your car blocking the track and stand next to it. When he reaches you, he'll slow down and call out, at which point you should press L2 to focus on him and use the "Mislead" dialogue option to ask for help. In my version, Lucia was wearing a ski-mask and had a baseball bat, which quickly convinced them all to run away (after a few swings), but either way, once he stops it's easy to steal the car. The baseball bat probably wasn't necessary, but hey, it's still non-lethal. As you exit the swamp, you'll get shot at and pursued by a few of his friends, but the BF Bandito is fast enough to outrun them easily. Bring it back to Moses to get $3,400ish as reward, though this may vary based on condition. sources.text: You need to find a way to steal the BF Bandito in Grand Theft Auto 6 to help out Moses. sources.text: Warning: this story features spoilers for an optional side activity. Those two chilling words were so soft I wondered if I'd heard them correctly – after all, the only souls in this orchard were me and Tootsie, an escaped cow draped in red cloth with a rosette stuck to her forehead. But no, I had heard them, and I turned them over in my head as I led Tootsie back along her rampaging path, through fallen fruit, over a busted wooden fence, and to her owner, a dairy farmer I'd found on the side of the road, flustered and crying about his prized $2 million show cow. I was still processing those two words as we approached the farmer's trailer, and when he told me that tonight, a fan had paid to watch a private Tootsie mud bath, I knew what I had to do. I shooed her to her freedom – "Go, run! Live your best life!" – and she galloped, ribbons fluttering, hooves pounding into the distance. To freedom rather than a busy highway, I hoped. I was Jason, the good Samaritan (if you ignore the part where I then provoked the farmer to start a fight, knocked him out cold, stamped on his limp body and stole the $500 in his pocket). This was about six hours into Rockstar's latest masterpiece . For a game as vast and open as GTA 6 , I found the opening strangely claustrophobic – to begin, the giant map of Leonida is shrouded in fog apart from the sliver of the Florida Keys where Jason lives and some surrounding swamp land. Key Lento is so dense with activities, shops, missions, and random encounters, not to mention the constant distraction of pottering around Jason's waterside house, that I felt overwhelmed by it all. And so, perhaps earlier than the game wanted me to, I pointed Jason's red pickup north and started driving. What I found was that GTA 6's open world holds delights that you can enjoy no matter where you are in the main story. I slipped west of Vice City, turning off the highway's spiralling spaghetti junctions near Buckskin Swamp. Soon I parked up at Emerald Springs, a nature reserve with pristine boardwalks and stands selling orange juice and doughnuts. I plodded the planks, eating a sandwich from the Black Bear Deli. I studied some ducks, beat up an entitled British tourist, stole a bike, and pedalled back to my car. I had hoped to find something crafted and scripted, but the fact that I could still have fun in a place with ostensibly nothing to do fills me with hope for the rest of the game. It was stark how, in just a few minutes of driving from Key Lento, the atmosphere had shifted completely, from road rage to tranquility. The beauty of the place and the amusing conversations to eavesdrop were captivating, even without a weird or wonderful encounter. I placed another waypoint vaguely northeast. It was on the way that I met Tootsie for what was undoubtedly the strangest moment I've had so far in GTA 6. Not only did it imply that animals could talk in this world, or at least psychically communicate, but that Jason could hear them. I wonder if that means anything. My detour from the main story had been worth it for Tootise (and the $500 from her owner) but it was barely lunchtime. GTA 6's extended day-night cycle feels central to how you play: you can get so much more done in a day than in Red Dead Redemption 2, and even after a languid morning routine of working out and coffee, you're still out the door before 08:00am. Low on gas, I rolled into a forecourt in Ambrosia, a town where abandoned factories and containers made way for quaint high streets. I was rewarded with another unique scene. A chap with a camo shirt and teeth like a Donegal graveyard spraying gasoline into a bathtub inexplicably mounted in the back of his pickup. "None of your regulations or mind control is going to stop me!" he shouted as the liquid sloshed down his tailgate, coating the dozen bumper stickers and dripping onto his boots. "I can pump gasoline wherever I want." He even sprayed it on Jason, and it took the threat of nearby sirens to hold me back. Thankfully, his cigarette did the work instead, falling and lighting the gas on fire, the flames engulfing his feet. "Those cigarettes'll kill ya man," Jason said, smirking. Every scripted random encounter so far has felt deliciously crafted. Some funny, some nightmarish. I like that they vary in length and level of interactivity so that when one starts, you never know if it'll trigger an actual quest or just puff into nothingness. I could've just watched the gas station spectacle unfold, like a mini stage play, but hours later when I found a tiger mauling bodies in an abandoned swamp hotel, I had to act. Later, I ambled a row of cafes and restaurants, got a haircut, ate a protein bar, and threw the protein bar wrapper at a guy who looked at me funny, sparking a seven-person brawl that drew the attention of a cops and – when I gunned one officer down – a police chopper. I was forced to flee even further north, driving along some railtracks and into the wilderness, not able to stop at the wonderfully named Thrillbully Mud Club. I eventually lost the police chopper and looped back to Ambrosia as the sun dawdled. I wanted to get back by bedtime but I didn't fancy the seven-mile drive back to Key Lento, and as if Rockstar was reading my thoughts, the next corner I rounded revealed a hospital complete with a helipad. I climbed into the cockpit, apologising silently to the next poor sod who needed airlifting to safety, and flew south. I could have seen this all later in the game. And perhaps I would have gotten more out of it if I'd waited another six hours: I haven't yet done a full robbery, and I'm sure Ambrosia is littered with potential targets. I've only controlled Lucia for one mission, and I'd love to see what happens if both protagonists find something strange together. But the day of distractions, a break from quests, was exactly what I needed, and I was feeling glad that Rockstar doesn't restrict where you can go from the start. I realise that "go and explore" is

sources.title: Should you shake Mattia's hand in GTA 6?
sources.text: Shaking Mattia's hand seems like quite an important moment in GTA 6 The chance to shake Mattia's hand in GTA 6 comes up right at the start of the mission Day Release, seemingly like a key decision that might affect the tone of the rest of the mission and future job prospects. Multiple GamesRadar+ writers have gone through both options, and it's a lot less important of a decision in GTA 6 than you think, so here's what we know about the significance of shaking Mattia's hand. Be aware of some very mild spoilers for later missions in Chapter 1 below. Shaking Mattia's hand in GTA 6 makes no difference to any events in the Day Release mission . If you shake his hand, you shake his hand, and if you don't, you don't. Mattia doesn't even acknowledge that you left him hanging. Later in the mission, Mattia offers Jason and Lucia some drugs in a nightclub and, again, accepting or refusing has no clear repercussions. Comparing videos of the choices side-by-side, there were no obvious differences between either outcome as the same thing happens regardless - Mattia either takes the drugs back or hands them over, stands up and leaves, then Jason and Lucia take to the dancefloor. The rest of the mission then plays out as normal. As far as I can tell, turning Mattia down in either of these situations in Day Release has no long-term impact either as the "job" that he mentions at the end of the mission is critical to the story and can't be avoided. Just make sure you've done everything before the GTA 6 Tourist Trap mission as it's an important one – and if you get stuck, my GTA 6 Tourist Trap walkthrough can help. sources.title: How to Get Ready for November 19
sources.text: November 19, 2026, has long been circled on your calendar. Birthdays, anniversaries, and holidays have come and gone, but this day belongs to you and your XBOX console. We can hardly believe it’s almost here, either. Once midnight strikes, you want to be locked in the action, so to help you prepare, we created a checklist to ensure distractions are put to bed so you can settle in for a season of gaming like nothing you’ve ever experienced before. 2026 has been full of some absolute bangers: Gears of War E-Day, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, Forza Horizon 6, Halo: Campaign Evolved, Minecraft Dungeons II, Diablo 4: Lord of Hatred , Control Resonant , Mixtape , Pragmata , The Blood of Dawnwalker , Star Wars: Galactic Racer , 007 First Light , Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve … seriously, all these games came out this year . That also means you might have a hard drive that is nearing capacity. And you will be faced with some hard choices to free up approximately 212GB of space on your XBOX Series X|S before November 19. You could always upgrade the capacity of your console to keep all your games at the ready, using the storage expansion slot on the back of the console. Otherwise, you’ll have a hard choice to make which we do not envy. But know that you’re in good company – we had to find a way to make room too. XBOX Cloud Gaming means that you don’t need to own an XBOX Series X|S console to experience the latest games (or use up that hard drive space) – you can stream directly from the cloud to your XBOX One console. Game Pass subscribers receive an allotment of hours per month as part of their plans, but you can also purchase blocks of time . Certain upcoming major releases have been confirmed as cloud-ready on day one , so even if you don’t own a current gen console, your latest obsession isn’t out of reach. You never want to settle in for a long gaming session only to immediately get hit with an update download. If you haven’t used your XBOX Series X|S or XBOX One in a minute, be sure to power up and connect to the internet beforehand and make sure you’re all set with the latest system updates. You can also install any upcoming releases you may have pre-ordered, while you’re at it. If you’re feeling a gaming flu coming on (and there’s a lot of that going around right now), then take a sick day, rather than risk infecting your coworkers or classmates. Sometimes you just need to listen to your body’s needs, relax, and let the fever run its course. Miami’s own DJ Khaled, aka Dr. XBOX will write you a personalized note to help explain the situation. If this thing is really serious, you may even need the whole week to recover – it’s the responsible thing to do. We all have responsibilities. Some of them come with four legs and a suspect bladder. Don’t let Rufus ruin your gaming fun. Get ahold of a local dog walker to take them outside so you can enjoy the big day uninterrupted. Or drop them off at doggie daycare for a day (or week) to get them out of your hair. Is your XBOX in an area of the house that is easily accessible to younger players? Consider the steps you need to take to get it out of younger sightlines, like running an extension cable out to the shed in the backyard or huddling up in your at-home office. Even if you do find yourself bouncing between rooms, your save files reside in the Cloud, allowing you to pick up your session wherever you last plugged your console in. We’re always on the hunt for new tunes and one of the things we’re most looking forward to on November 19 is discovering a whole bunch of new tracks that are sure to make our listening playlist pop throughout the year. You can get started here on Spotify . XBOX Design Lab lets you create your own next-gen XBOX Wireless Controller. Choose from a combination of colors, patterns, textured grips, and more. You could even pick up some specially themed versions of controllers styled in hot pink and pastels – this one is particularly striking . Speaking of controllers, if you expect long gaming sessions in your near future, make sure that it’s plugged in so it has a full charge when you need it, or stock up on AA batteries. Maybe even get a backup controller ready so you can hot-swap them in and minimize interruptions. Looking for something to add to your queue? Check out the 1967 classic, “Bonnie and Clyde,” featuring Warren Beatty and Faye Dunaway to get you in the mood for an epic story about two tragic lovers who fall into a life of crime. We’ll have to wait and see if the outcome is any different this time around starting on November 19.

sources.text: Finding the Slim Jim in Chapter 2 is essential if you want to get better at stealing vehicles Stealing cars in GTA 6 is one of the easiest ways to attract attention from the police, thanks to the new Wanted system. You've probably noticed by now that breaking into vehicles is noisy and messy, with Jason and Lucia needing to smash the window to get inside. It also takes time – precious time in which some nosey onlooker can report your description and activity to the cops. There has to be an easier way, right? There is. Which is why you need to learn how to get a Slim Jim in GTA 6. The Slim Jim in GTA 6 is only available from Chapter 2 onwards. This essential carjacking tool will unlock as part of the main GTA 6 mission list , coming into your possession after you begin a quest called ' Moses '. It's in this mission where you'll meet your first vehicle fence, learn how to sell cars and bikes in GTA 6 , and be given the information you need to better survey vehicles for security features with the WAiNK app – which can be activated at any time by holding Up on the D-pad. Moses will give you the Slim Jim as a part of this mission. It'll let you get into any vehicle without needing to smash the window. You will, however, still need to contend with security features – you'll have to wait until Chapter 3 to learn how to get the Key Cloner in GTA 6 and understand how to deactivate trackers to steal more modern vehicles. Once you've got it, using the Slim Jim is GTA 6 is easy enough. Walk up to any vehicle you want to try and steal. Walk up to the driver-side or passenger door, and press Triangle/Y to bring out your Slim Jim. From there, it's a case of rotating the right thumbstick in a curve until you find the sweet spot – which you'll spot by rumble in the controller and by a slightly pink hue to the semi-circle indicator. sources.text: If you want to get in and out of a heist as fast as possible, here's how to get GTA 6 safe codes Finding and inputting GTA 6 safe codes is a slicker way to break into the 50+ safes scattered throughout the GTA 6 map . While some safes can be opened with sheer brute force, those that require a code often offer more lucrative rewards, so finding these safe codes can be a great way to make cash fast in GTA 6 . Unfortunately, these safe codes aren't always easy to come by. While some of the safe codes in GTA 6 are set – with those critical to the story and major side missions always consisting of the same digits– many of the codes are randomized and can change from player to player. So, while I can't give you the codes for those safes, I can at least help by guiding you on how to obtain them. sources.text: The GTA 6 Snap Tool is an essential item which lets you get into locked doors without setting off alarms Breaking and entering is more complicated than it's ever been before in a Grand Theft Auto game. You never know what's behind a locked door – cash to be grabbed, narcotics to be fences, safes to be broken into. The problem is that breaking open doors creates a lot of noise, and will set off alarms. Thankfully, there is another way. All you need is to find the Snap Gun in GTA 6. The Snap Gun is a lockpicking device that can be acquired by progressing through the main story, and it's perhaps the most important piece of equipment in the game (beating out the Slim Jim and the Key Cloner ). Below I'm going to walk you through how to get the GTA 6 Snap Gun and how to use it. The Snap Gun is locked behind progression. You'll need to complete Yasmani's Jewelry Jobs in Chapter 3, a fence-specific GTA 6 mission that unlocks after you've completed Boobie Time. You'll be introduced to Yasmani, one of the key vendors in GTA 6 who will pay a premium for marked bills and jewellery you've stolen. He'll give you the Snap Gun so that Jason and Lucia can properly assist in a few heists of high-end jewellery stores in Vice City. If a door is locked, there's a very good chance that you can use the Snap Gun to open it. Walk up to a door and, rather than pressing Square/X to break it open, press Triangle/Y instead. This will let you use the Snap Gun, where you're then required to use the left analogue stick to find the sweet spot and then pump the right-trigger until a meter fills. You'll hear the click when the lock is picked. The Snap Gun is particularly useful when you're robbing Pawn Shops, Jewellery stores, and other key locations – so long as you've already threatened the clerks and guards to stay still while you work. The Snap gun circumvents alarm systems installed in stores to monitor the door. It's worth noting here that in certain locations that carry a lot of cash or valuables, a Snap Gun won't be enough. If you walk up to a door and it's only asking for explosives, then a sticky bomb or grenade is what's required – just prepared for the alarms to go off and for the cops to be in hot pursuit. sources.title: How to get a GTA 6 Rhino tank and become virtually indestructible
sources.text: There are rows of GTA 6 tanks waiting to be liberated right from the start of the game, to earn the Challenging Tank award Getting a tank in GTA 6 represents the pinnacle of criminal behavior, and there's a long history of stealing Rhinos going all the way back through the series to GTA 3! These military vehicles are virtually indestructible so you're safely protected inside, and they pack a powerful enough punch with their cannon to destroy anything GTA 6 puts in front of you. You also need to get inside one to unlock the Challenging Tank Trophy or Achievement, so to help you out with that, here's how to steal a tank in GTA 6. The location for an entire row of GTA 6 tanks is in the Mile Zero Air Station, situated west of the area you begin the story in, which you can reach by driving through Abismo Key and on to Southwind. You'll need a vehicle to break into the military base which will get left behind, so it's best not to use your GTA 6 personal vehicle for this job, and equipping body armor from Ammu-nation is highly recommended for added protection. By following the route marked on my map above you'll weave through several road barriers, as which point the soldiers will open fire on you, then turn right at the first opportunity to pass more barriers and soldiers until you spot a handy pile of dirt. You must use this Stunt Jump to clear the perimeter fence, though if you don't get enough height to also clear the inner fence you can smash through it to reach the runway. Look to your left when on the miliary runway and you'll see a large building, and to the left of that are the Rhino tanks we're looking for – you can also head to the right of that building if you'd prefer to grab a GTA 6 jet instead. Once you reach the tanks, crash through the fence and then approach one before using the usual enter vehicle button to climb in through the front hatch. Note that there is various military hardware in this area, but the Rhino tanks are the ones closest to the fence you broke through. You can then drive away in your new GTA 6 tank, which will shortly unlock the Challenging Tank award from the GTA 6 Trophy and Achievement list to add to your collection. Strangely, commandeering this military vehicle doesn't initially increase your GTA 6 Wanted Level beyond the existing two-stars for breaking into the base, though this soon goes to five and then six-stars when you start blasting things with your cannon. Don't expect to get too far in your Rhino tank, as it drives pretty slowly and you're being constantly peppered with incoming gunfire plus rockets from helicopters – which you can shoot down if you aim your barrel high enough. sources.title: How to get Arthur Morgan's Hat in GTA 6
sources.text: Arthur Morgan's genuine cowboy hat is found in a yard sale. Arthur Morgan's hat is found in GTA 6, a genuine cowboy hat that serves as a easter egg and reference to Red Dead Redemption 2, Rockstar's previous game and sibling franchise to Grand Theft Auto. Not just found on a hook somewhere, Arthur's Hat can actually be purchased and added to Jason and Lucia's wardrobe permanently - if you know the location of who's selling it. To get Arthur Morgan's brown leather cowboy hat for yourself in GTA 6, you need to go to a yard sale in the South of Port Gellhorn, found at the location marked above. The sale is marked by several very obvious balloons floating outside. Once there, head to the couch at the end, where you'll see a guitar case and a hat resting on it. That's Arthur Morgan's hat, though GTA 6 calls it a "Genuine Cowboy Hat" in Brown Leather. You can buy it from the owner, though the price seems to vary. When I bought it, it was $35, though some online have reported it being cheaper than that, suggesting the cost might be randomised. Once purchased, the hat will be in your wardrobe and clothing inventory permanently! For a little easter egg has the seller mention that she has no idea where the hat came from: perhaps she's a descendant of John Marston, the last canonical owner of that hat? This region will be a lot easier to access once you reach chapter 2. To see how far you are from that point if you haven't reached it yet, check out our GTA 6 Mission list . sources.title: How a $6 Beer in GTA 6 Sent Me Into a Spiral of Crime and Anxiety
sources.text: I'm relationship-maxxing GTA 6. Forget the money, the cars, or building a criminal empire. My main aim is to make Jason and Lucia so disgustingly loved up that NPCs violently vomit as we walk past being all cute together. I want them to be the perfect couple. I want romance. I want devotion. I want the sort of relationship that makes everyone else in Vice City feel deeply inadequate. Unfortunately, the nuanced way GTA 6 tracks even the smallest actions has turned me into a paranoid lunatic, constantly worrying that one wrong move will destroy my carefully cultivated romance. Case in point: a $6 beer that sent me into a cascade of disasters, petty crime, and emotional turmoil, eventually ending with me restarting an entire mission because I was worried I'd blown it. Early on in the game, you're given the chance to prepare the house and complete some simple objectives ahead of picking Lucia up from prison. Naturally, I did them all. Fixed the steps, bought the necklace, got the flowers. I even made sure the car was dent-free, had a haircut and a shower, and dressed my Jason in his best jeans and shirt. My man was going to look presentable when he picked up the love of his life. I was on my best behavior. Nothing was going to stop me getting to my girl. In fact, I was so determined to be the perfect boyfriend that I even avoided committing any crimes on the way to the prison. In Grand Theft Auto. I obeyed traffic laws. I stopped at red lights. I avoided trouble wherever possible, to the point that when a random NPC tried to mug me, I just handed over my cash rather than risk getting into a fight. Remember that last part. It's important. After picking Lucia up from prison, you head straight to the Rusty Anchor for a few drinks. So far, so good. We've got the flowers, the necklace, the freshly showered boyfriend. This is going brilliantly. Then Lucia wanders off for a moment and asks Jason to get her a drink. Shit. I have no money. Suddenly, my decision to be a law-abiding citizen has come back to bite me in the arse. I gave all my money to a mugger because I was trying to be a good boyfriend, and now I can't afford to buy my girlfriend a beer. A beer that costs just $6. Surely this is a relationship test? If I follow Lucia without her drink, am I getting a little broken heart icon? Is this going into some invisible ledger of romantic failures? Have I already failed as a boyfriend, future husband, and potential co-parent because I can't produce one lousy alcoholic beverage? I start looking for solutions. I check every bottle in the bar, hoping I can just grab one and pretend I've paid for it. They're all empty. I search the entire building for something I could quickly pawn, like a trading card, or even just some random cash someone has carelessly left lying around. Nothing. The panic is setting in. I head outside and start searching the nearby streets. I don't want a wanted rating, because surely being arrested while Lucia waits patiently for a drink isn't going to do wonders for our relationship either. So I look for cars with trunks I can break into easily. I find a selection of sunglasses and hats, which is lovely, but unless Lucia has suddenly developed a taste for drinking accessories, they're not going to help me. I'm now seriously considering mugging someone. I only need $6. Six. Dollars. That's barely a crime, right? In the grand scheme of GTA, that's practically community service. I pull out my gun and start advancing on a random NPC walking down the sidewalk. I'm about to threaten an innocent stranger with a deadly weapon so I can buy my girlfriend a beer. This is what love looks like, apparently. And then it happens. The game suddenly switches to a cutscene of Lucia saying, "You forgot about me?" NO. NO! The opposite! I was thinking about you the entire time! I needed $6 for a beer, light of my life! I was prepared to commit armed robbery for you! Does that mean nothing? But the damage is done. Or at least, I think the damage is done, which is somehow worse. Has the game registered that I wandered off and abandoned Lucia? Does she think Jason is an inconsiderate arsehole? Have I just knocked several invisible points off my perfect relationship score? Is this going to come back to haunt me 30 hours from now when she remembers that time I left her alone in a bar? I can't take the risk. I restart the checkpoint. Unfortunately, this creates another problem. The checkpoint puts me right outside the prison, which means I still have no money. I've travelled back in time, but I haven't solved the fundamental issue of being a broke boyfriend. Luckily, there's a parking lot nearby. This time, I abandon my commitment to good behaviour. I go rogue, breaking open trunks left and right, ignoring alarms and grabbing whatever I can get my hands on. The same man who was carefully obeying traffic laws 20 minutes ago is now systematically robbing parked cars in broad daylight. Eventually, I walk away with $30. A fortune. Five beers' worth of romantic security. I get Lucia her drink. Crisis averted. Relationship saved. Probably. And that's the thing about GTA 6 that's completely got its hooks into me. I've become so thoroughly relationship-pilled that I'm making decisions I would never normally consider in a Grand Theft Auto game. I'm not thinking about how much money I can make, how many cars I can steal, or how much chaos I can cause. I'm thinking about whether Jason is being a good boyfriend. I'm worrying about whether Lucia feels appreciated. I'm committing crimes not for personal gain, but in the service of being a thoughtful romantic partner. It's ridiculous, but it's also fascinating. Rockstar has somehow made me care about the smallest interactions between these two characters to the point where I'm second-guessing everything I do. The possibility that an apparently insignificant action might have consequences for their relationship is enough to make even buying a beer feel like a high-stakes

sources.title: Learn how to get a mask in GTA 6 to stay anonymous when committing a crime
sources.text: Learning how to buy, manage, and equip a mask in GTA 6 is vital for losing some of your Appearance Heat If you want to be a better criminal in Leonida, you're going to need to learn how to get a mask in GTA 6. Despite Rockstar making appearance a key factor in the new Wanted system, the game isn't super clear on the steps you can take to hide your identity – particularly as you're progressing through Chapter 1 of the GTA 6 missions list . Thankfully, I'm here to help you understand how to get neckwear in GTA 6 , how to equip masks, and how to change them for new ones. You can buy a mask in GTA 6 from any of the gun stores. Chuck's Tackle & Shot in Key Lento sells them (look at the central stand with the alligator head atop of it) from the beginning of the game, but you can head to any Ammu-Nation retailer to find more. Open up the GTA 6 Index , head into the weapons tab, and you'll be able to find all the relevant shops on your map. When you begin exploring Vice City and Vice Beach, you'll also find thrift stores that sell novelty masks, and high-end retailers which sell very fancy (and expensive) coverings that can be worn as well. To wear a mask in GTA 6, you need to make sure that it's with you. You can add neckwear items to your loadout by visiting the wardrobe in your residences. Scroll to the accessories tab and that's where you'll find the Masks option, which separates them by brand. If you want options while you're on the road, you can also store some in the trunk of your personal vehicle in GTA 6 by highlighting it and pressing Square/X. With a mask in your loadout, wearing it is as simple as holding L1/LB to open your loadout. Press R1/RB to scroll to the items menu, and then select Mask from the neckwear slot located at twelve-o'clock in the wheel. Press A to put it on, press A to remove it. Easy enough, and vital if you want to lose some of your Appearance Heat after robbing a store with CCTV equipment. While hovering over the neckwear slot of your loadout, you can also press up and down to change the wear style of your mask in GTA 6. The first will see the mask conceal your face, which will draw panicked reactions from shop clerks, while the second will let you fashion the mask more appropriately. sources.title: Arknights: Endfield version update ‘Meeting You in the World o’Shrooms’ launches November 25
sources.text: Publisher GRYPHLINE and developer Mountain Contour will release the version update “Meeting You in the World o’Shrooms” for free-to-play 3D RPG Arknights: Endfield on November 25, the companies announced. The game’s latest live stream also introduced the upcoming version 2.0 update, which takes players to Gypsosia and aboard the Rhodes Island landship, and teased 10 characters who will join the journey across upcoming content updates. “With Wuling’s story wrapping up, and the main story taking us through all the heavy moments, we want to give you a change of pace with a lighthearted, upbeat update,” said Arknights: Endfield producer Light Zhong in a press release. Here is an overview of the update, via GRYPHLINE: Version Update “Meeting You in the World o’Shrooms” Strange mushrooms have overrun an abandoned dam outside Wuling, where Landbreakers worship a giant mushroom and visitors keep slipping into hallucinations. There, the Endministrator meets Kay, a Rhodes Island Operator who has been adventuring alone across Talos-II in search of them. Kay happily shares everything she treasures, including a towering stack of honey waffles. But which would she choose: a mountain of waffles or a dear friend? A Nature Vanguard with a carefree fighting style, Kay throws weapons that scatter across the battlefield, then gathers them up for a heavy hammer slam. Along the way, she drops Picnic Snacks that heal her teammates. The Old Dam, the update’s new area, has grown into a fairytale-like mushroom kingdom. Players fire Kay’s honey waffles at mushrooms to open doors and spin fungal bridges, and must avoid Loquacious Shrooms that scramble their sense of direction. Mushroom foes like the Bolete Prince guard the dam, and a mushroom as tall as a mountain waits at its heart. The update’s music leans into its whimsical tone, with Ori composer Gareth Coker and ambient producer Owsey returning to score Kay’s honey waffle adventure. It caps a first year in which the soundtrack has followed the story, from the sweeping sci-fi orchestral sound of Valley IV to the choir-driven battle against Alleikhreos, Typhoeus’s JRPG-inspired winter journey and the modern electronic take on Eastern music in Si’s painted world. Later in the update, every player who logs in during the Workers’ Guards: Roll Call event will receive the Operator Mimino and her signature weapon, Star of Tomorrow, for free, with event missions offering extra copies to reach full Potential. Operators Gilberta and Rossi also return in successive reruns. For factory builders, Exclusion Zone Rebuilding is a new permanent mode in which players supply materials across four phases to restore the North Wuling Exclusion Zone, using the new Forge of Luminance to transform products on their conveyor belts. For a lighter break, Lucky Carrot’s Games of Wonder adds two multiplayer card games, Witch’s Darkjack and Band Uprising, that players can enjoy with friends or through matchmaking. A First Look at Version 2.0 and Rhodes Island The livestream also previewed the next chapter of Arknights: Endfield , arriving in the new year. Exiles have launched attacks across the Civilization Band, and their real target is Rhodes Island. The Endministrator sets out with Perlica into Gypsosia, the Cretaceous Frontiers, where players will be able to board and explore Rhodes Island itself, a massive landship. A 10-character teaser offered a glimpse of companions for the journey, including Warfarin, appearing as the leader of Rhodes Island, and M3, who returns looking completely different. The chapter’s first update will add four new maps at once, including Rhodes Island. Main Mission Early Unlock: Gypsosia will let players who have completed the main mission Remediation Progress skip ahead to the new story while still earning all beginner-event rewards. New modes are also in development for future updates, including a management sim with the Golden Branch Tribe and the Shattered Protocol combat mode. Arknights: Endfield is now Steam Deck Verified, with default controller support and every feature available on Valve’s handheld. The update also brings Despot Weaponized, a new high-difficulty challenge series in Umbral Monument; the return of RISE! MEGA ARENA!, a two-Operator arena event; and new seasons of the Echoes of War combat mode. Arknights: Endfield is available now for PlayStation 5 , PC via the official launcher, Steam , and Epic Games Store , iOS via App Store , and Android via Google Play .

sources.text: Domingo é dia da nossa lista de lançamentos de jogos, para que você possa programar a sua agenda nos próximos dias. E o destaque dessa vez é Arkheron , game desenvolvido por um dos criadores de World of Warcraft e que mistura elementos de ação em tempo real com estratégia e coleta de itens ao longo das fases. Outro destaque é Appulse. O game conta com uma proposta ousada de misturar elementos de ação em tempo real, mais precisamente no controle de naves, a uma espécie de mesa de pinball interativa. Confira a lista completa de lançamentos da semana e os respectivos preços. Athelan Battlegrounds é um jogo de estratégia tática por turnos desenvolvido por uma equipe independente de duas pessoas. A proposta mistura elementos de xadrez com mecânicas de jogos competitivos em arenas, colocando os jogadores para montar equipes e disputar partidas estratégicas contra outros oponentes online. O título aposta em um sistema competitivo baseado apenas na habilidade dos participantes , sem mecânicas de progressão que ofereçam vantagens fora das partidas ou recursos pagos que influenciem o resultado. O game será distribuído de forma gratuita no PC através do Steam e já conta com uma versão demo para download. Appulse é um jogo de tiro com visão superior inspirado nas mecânicas clássicas de pinball. Ambientado no espaço, você precisa assumir o controle de uma nave e, assim, dominar o recuo das armas para controlar a trajetória da esfera pelo tabuleiro enquanto protege sua nave-mãe contra ondas de robôs invasores. A cada nível alcançado, é possível escolher melhorias para personalizar o arsenal, as habilidades e os recursos da mesa , além de utilizar um canhão de ejeção para invadir naves inimigas e cumprir objetivos específicos. O jogo ainda não possui um preço definido, mas já conta com uma versão demo disponível de forma gratuita. Arkheron é um jogo de ação isométrico focado em partidas competitivas entre equipes. A dinâmica consiste em escalar uma torre ao lado de dois aliados, enfrentando outros grupos de jogadores e coletando equipamentos pelo caminho que alteram as habilidades e a forma de jogar no meio dos combates. O título, que foi desenvolvido pelo veterano de World of Warcraft , Rob Pardo, também contará com um visual repleto de detalhes, além de um sistema de ranqueamento para possíveis torneios no futuro. O jogo ainda não possui um preço definido, mas é possível se inscrever para o período de testes, que ainda está em andamento. E na sua opinião, qual o game mais esperado da semana?
